explanation: Locate the selected node, copy its successor’s value into it, then bypass that successor. After locating the node, deletion uses only that node and its successor, as requested; the selected position cannot be the tail.
timeComplexity: O(index+1): traverse index links, then perform one data copy and one bypass.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Replacing the selected node’s value with its successor’s value and bypassing that successor yields exactly the value sequence obtained by deleting the selected position. Once the position is located, no predecessor is consulted, which is the required deletion technique.
walkthrough: For [7,5,9,2] and selected position 1, copy 9 into the node containing 5, then bypass the former 9 node. The resulting value sequence is [7,9,2].
edgeCases: The selected node cannot be the tail.
Selecting the head is permitted by this exercise.
The method intentionally changes the selected node’s stored value.
